metadata.purpose: Architecture context for AI coding agents and maintainers.
accuracyNotes: Facts are derived from source files in this repository, package metadata, README documentation, and local Supabase migrations.

framework.name: Next.js
framework.renderingModel: React Server Components with many client-component route islands

ui.stylingModel: Tailwind utilities with shadcn-style CSS variables and reusable UI primitives

supporting: pg_cron and pg_net for scheduled sale polling

deployment.target: Vercel-shaped Next.js deployment with Supabase hosted services

root.name: Application root layout
root.role: Defines global metadata, font, theme provider, Thirdweb/MetaMask providers, and toast provider.

root.name: Home page
root.role: Landing page wrapped in the main layout.

root.name: Middleware
root.role: Creates Supabase SSR client, refreshes sessions, redirects legacy paths, protects selected routes, and checks admin role.

components.name: Layout Shell
components.responsibility: Shared page chrome, navigation, dashboard framing, and wallet status presentation.

components.name: Authentication UI
components.responsibility: Email/password auth, signup, profile synchronization, wallet auth surfaces, and client session state.

components.name: NFT and Artwork UI
components.responsibility: Artwork upload, gallery cards, NFT management, artwork detail/edit views, and mint/sell actions.

components.name: Wallet and Web3 Layer
components.responsibility: MetaMask connection, Thirdweb provider setup, chain helpers, wallet display, and legacy web3-react connector support.

components.name: Supabase Data Access
components.responsibility: Browser/server Supabase clients, typed database access, auth guards, profile lookup, storage upload helpers, and cart/artwork APIs.

components.name: Cart Store
components.responsibility: Client cart state persisted by Zustand and synchronized through Supabase API helper functions.

dataFlows.name: Supabase Auth Session Flow
steps: User submits auth forms in client components.
useAuth and Supabase browser client establish a session.
Middleware creates a Supabase SSR client and calls auth.getUser on matched page requests.
Server utilities use cookies() with @supabase/ssr for RSC/API access.
Admin requests additionally query users.role before allowing access.

dataFlows.name: Artwork Upload Flow
steps: Seller enters artwork metadata and PHP price in upload UI.
Client validates form data and uploads image to Supabase Storage.
Client creates artwork row in Supabase Postgres.
Artwork appears in account/dashboard/gallery surfaces based on status and ownership.

dataFlows.name: Mint Approval Flow
steps: Seller or UI creates a mint request for artwork.
Admin reviews requests in admin dashboard.
Approval API mints or records NFT token data through Thirdweb/blockchain helpers.
Token ID and transaction metadata are stored in Supabase.

dataFlows.name: Sell Request and OpenSea Listing Flow
steps: Seller creates a sell request after minting.
Admin approval API converts PHP pricing to WETH and calls OpenSea listing service.
Server-side OpenSea SDK signs with admin wallet credentials.
Artwork stores listing URL/status in Supabase.

dataFlows.name: Automated Sale Detection and Notification Flow
steps: pg_cron invokes the Supabase Edge Function every minute through pg_net.
Edge Function authenticates the x-cron-secret from Vault/env.
Function polls OpenSea sale events for listed NFTs.
RPC records sold status and enqueues a notification outbox item.
Function claims pending outbox rows and sends seller/admin emails through Resend.

dataFlows.name: Collection Cache and Queue Flow
steps: Collection endpoints read/write collection metadata.
Cache and process-queue route handlers use Vercel KV.
Supabase tables and OpenSea/Alchemy APIs provide backing data.

dataFlows.name: Cart and Checkout Flow
steps: Client cart state lives in Zustand with local persistence.
Cart mutations call Supabase API helper functions.
Checkout and orders pages consume persisted database state.

constraints.name: Environment configuration is required for most runtime paths
constraints.details: Supabase URL/anon key/service role, Polygon RPC, OpenSea API key, Thirdweb admin credentials, Resend keys, Vercel KV, and app URLs are required by different subsystems.

constraints.name: Middleware does not protect API routes
constraints.details: The middleware matcher excludes api, so each route handler must enforce its own auth and authorization.

constraints.name: Supabase RLS controls exposed data access
constraints.details: Local migrations enable RLS for users/storage/collections, but app queries imply joins that may need additional hosted policies.

constraints.name: Architecture map is self-contained
constraints.details: The generated HTML does not rely on CDN scripts, external CSS, or network data.

architectureDecisions.decision: Use Next.js App Router with server pages and client islands.
tradeoffs: Several whole-route client pages increase bundle size and client-side auth reliance.

architectureDecisions.decision: Use Supabase for auth, relational data, object storage, edge jobs, secrets, and scheduled sale polling.
tradeoffs: Keeps most backend state in one platform.
Local generated types and migrations must stay synchronized with hosted state.

architectureDecisions.decision: Create OpenSea listings server-side using an admin wallet and OpenSea SDK.
tradeoffs: Requires sensitive credentials and robust environment validation.

architectureDecisions.decision: Sellers enter PHP prices; listing flow converts to WETH for OpenSea.
tradeoffs: Requires accurate exchange rate handling and clear price-change messaging.

architecturalIssues.title: Middleware redirects all /marketplace paths to /gallery
architecturalIssues.details: The middleware redirects both /marketplace and /marketplace/... to /gallery, which can make app/marketplace/[contract]/[tokenId] unreachable through direct navigation.

architecturalIssues.title: Three NFT detail URL patterns exist
architecturalIssues.details: NFT detail surfaces are split across /nft/[contractAddress]/[tokenId], /nfts/[contract]/[tokenId], and /marketplace/[contract]/[tokenId], increasing SEO, canonical URL, and maintenance risk.

architecturalIssues.title: Upload behavior is implemented in more than one place
architecturalIssues.details: Account upload and dashboard NFT upload use different route/component implementations with overlapping pricing and validation concerns.

architecturalIssues.title: Wallet integration uses multiple paradigms
architecturalIssues.details: The app mixes Thirdweb, MetaMask SDK, and web3-react connectors/hooks, which increases bundle size and behavioral drift.

architecturalIssues.title: OpenSea code paths use both ethers v5 and ethers v6
architecturalIssues.details: lib/services/opensea.ts and lib/opensea/listings.ts represent separate OpenSea/ethers entry points, making listing behavior harder to reason about.

architecturalIssues.title: Production build ignores TypeScript errors
architecturalIssues.details: next.config.js sets typescript.ignoreBuildErrors to true, allowing production builds to ship with type errors.

architecturalIssues.title: Next/Image allows any HTTPS hostname
architecturalIssues.details: next.config.js includes remotePatterns hostname '**', which reduces control over remote image origins.

architecturalIssues.title: Supabase project URL and NFT contract are hardcoded in runtime paths
architecturalIssues.details: The sale cron migration hardcodes a Supabase project URL, and listing/edge code duplicates a hardcoded NFT contract value instead of relying on a single environment source.

architecturalIssues.title: Generated Supabase types lag newer tables and RPCs
architecturalIssues.details: nft_sale_notifications and sale-notification RPCs are represented in migrations/edge code but not in lib/types/database.ts Functions/Tables.

architecturalIssues.title: Browser Supabase API helper attempts bucket administration
architecturalIssues.details: The storage helper attempts getBucket/createBucket through the browser client path, but bucket administration should generally be provisioned server-side or through setup scripts.

architecturalIssues.title: Wallet verification route has a fixed JWT secret fallback
architecturalIssues.details: The verify-wallet route was observed to fall back to a fixed secret if AUTH_PRIVATE_KEY is missing, which would be unsafe in production.

architecturalIssues.title: Deprecated Next cron endpoint remains in the route tree
architecturalIssues.details: The old /api/cron/poll-opensea-sales route returns 410 after sale polling moved to Supabase Edge + pg_cron; old schedulers must be removed.

recommendedNextActions.action: Re-enable TypeScript build enforcement after fixing current type errors.
Remove the fixed JWT secret fallback and fail closed when AUTH_PRIVATE_KEY is missing.
Choose a canonical NFT detail route and update middleware redirects so marketplace deep links are intentional.
Consolidate account/dashboard upload flows behind one shared form and server action/API contract.
Regenerate Supabase types from the active schema and include newer outbox/RPC definitions.
Pick one wallet/web3 integration model and retire duplicate connectors where possible.
Parameterize project URL and NFT contract values through environment or deployment-specific migrations.
